tb-210-4.question:
Two satellites P and Q move around the Earth in circular orbits. They have the same mass but the orbit of P has a larger radius. Which of the following statements about P and Q is/are correct?

(1) P has a shorter period than Q.

(2) P has a smaller acceleration towards the Earth’s centre than Q.

(3) P has a lower KE than Q.

A (1) and (2) only

B (1) and (3) only

C (2) and (3) only

D (1), (2) and (3)
tb-210-4.reasoning:
By ω =GMr3, as the orbital radius r of P is larger than that of Q, P has a lower angular speed ω, and hence a longer orbital period.

∴ (1) is incorrect.

By a = g =GMr2, as the orbital radius r of P is larger than that of Q, P has a smaller acceleration a than Q.

∴ (2) is correct.

By v =GMr, as the orbital radius r of P is larger than that of Q, P has a lower linear speed v and hence a lower KE than Q.

∴ (3) is correct.

tb-210-5.question:
Two satellites P and Q move around the Earth in circular orbits. Their orbits are of the same radius but P has a smaller mass. Which of the following statements about P and Q is/are correct?

(1) P has a shorter period than Q.

(2) P has a smaller acceleration towards the Earth’s centre than Q.

(3) P has a lower KE than Q.

A (3) only

B (1) and (2) only

C (1) and (3) only

D (2) and (3) only
tb-210-5.reasoning:
By ω =GMr3, as the two satellites have the same orbital radii r, their angular speeds ω and periods are the same.

∴ (1) is incorrect.

By a = g =GMr2, as the two satellites have the same orbital radii r, their accelerations a are the same.

∴ (2) is incorrect.

By v =GMr, as the two satellites have the same orbital radii r, their linear speeds v are the same.

By KE =12mv2, as P has a smaller mass m, P has a lower KE than Q.

∴ (3) is correct.

tb-210-7.question:
Two objects revolve around a planet in circular orbits. Which of the following statements about the two objects is/are correct?

(1) If their orbital radii are the same, the centripetal forces they need must be the same.

(2) If their orbital radii are the same, their orbital periods must be the same.

(3) Their orbits must lie on the same plane.

A (2) only

B (1) and (2) only

C (1) and (3) only

D (1), (2) and (3)
tb-210-7.reasoning:
By F =mv2r, the centripetal force F also depends on the mass m of the object.

∴ (1) is incorrect.

By ω =GMr3, if their orbital radii r are the same, they must have the same angular speeds ω and orbital periods.

∴ (2) is correct.

The orbits of the objects can lie on any plane passing through the centre of gravity of the planet and do not necessarily lie on the same plane.

∴ (3) is incorrect.

tb-210-10.question:
A satellite revolves around the Earth in a circular orbit. Which of the following statements about the gravitational force acting on the satellite is/ are correct?

(1) It is balanced by the centripetal force of the satellite.

(2) Its magnitude depends on the mass of the satellite.

(3) It has the same direction as the satellite’s velocity.

A (1) only

B (2) only

C (3) only

D (1) and (2) only
tb-210-10.reasoning:
Centripetal force is provided by gravitational force.

∴ (1) is incorrect.

By F =GMmr2, the magnitude of gravitational force F depends on the mass m of the satellite.

∴ (2) is correct.

The direction of velocity is tangential to the orbit while the gravitational force points towards the centre of the orbit.

∴ (3) is incorrect.

tb-210-12.question:
Imagine that a satellite moves in a circular orbit around the Earth very close to the Earth’s surface, i.e. at about 6370 km from the Earth’s centre. Which of the following about the orbital period of the satellite is correct?

A It is about 1 day.

B It is much longer than 1 day.

C It is much shorter than 1 day.

D Its value depends on the satellite’s mass.
tb-210-12.reasoning:
A satellite at the geostationary orbit has an orbital period of 1 day.

A satellite very close to the Earth’s surface has an orbit of a much smaller orbital radius r than the geostationary orbit. By ω =GMr3, the satellite has a much higher angular speed ω than that at the geostationary orbit.

Therefore, its period is much shorter than 1 day.
